subjects.displayTitle: Prayers for teaching: finding strength, wisdom, and a listening heart
subjects.introduction: A bird with a broken wing whose flight is slow, a gnat asking to be made an eagle, a drop hoping to become a sea: this is how ‘Abdu’l-Bahá taught those who set out to share their faith to describe themselves before God. The prayers He and Bahá’u’lláh gave to teachers are startling in their honesty about weakness. Not eloquence first, but wisdom and utterance together, so that what is said may draw people near; not victory over hearers, but the rending of their veils; strength for a weary body, the gathering of scattered affairs, companionship on foreign roads, and the grace to be taught while teaching. Moses asked for an opened breast, an eased task and a loosened tongue so that his speech could be understood, and that ancient petition sits naturally beside these [1]. Whoever prays this way soon finds the path leading into the call to teach, into teaching the Cause as a daily practice, and into the wider life of prayer from which such speaking draws its breath.
subjects.arc: Begin with the willingness to learn and the courage of a wounded bird, then explore wisdom, service to hearers, shared effort, perseverance, and prayerful speech.

order.why: Explore the transformation of limited capacity through assistance.
shortened: O my God! O my God! Thou seest me in my lowliness and weakness, occupied with the greatest undertaking, determined to raise Thy word among the masses and to spread Thy teachings among Thy peoples. How can I succeed unless Thou assist me with the breath of the Holy Spirit, help me to triumph by the hosts of Thy glorious kingdom, and shower upon me Thy confirmations, which alone can change a gnat into an eagle, a drop of water into rivers and seas, and an atom into lights and suns? O my Lord! Assist me with Thy triumphant and effective might, so that my tongue may utter Thy praises and attributes among all people and my soul overflow with the wine of Thy love and knowledge.

order.why: Open with the reciprocal desire to teach and be taught.
shortened: We are sightless - make us seeing. We are dead - bring us to life. We are alone - cherish us and be kind. Enable us to teach and be taught, and confirm us in study and perfection.

order.why: Give weakness a memorable form through the broken-winged bird.
shortened: O God! O God! This is a broken-winged bird and his flight is very slow---assist him so that he may fly toward the apex of prosperity and salvation, wing his way with the utmost joy and happiness throughout the illimitable space, raise his melody in Thy Supreme Name in all the regions, exhilarate the ears with this call, and brighten the eyes by beholding the signs of guidance.

O Lord! I am single, alone and lowly. For me there is no support save Thee, no helper except Thee and no sustainer beside Thee. Confirm me in Thy service, assist me with the cohorts of Thine angels, make me victorious in the promotion of Thy Word and suffer me to speak out Thy wisdom amongst Thy creatures. Verily, Thou art the helper of the weak and the defender of the little ones, and verily Thou art the Powerful, the Mighty and the Unconstrained.

order.why: Place shared teaching within humility toward others and unity among participants.
shortened: O God! O God! We are Thy humble and submissive servants, leaves of Thine exalted and verdant paradise, drops from the basins of Thine abundant mercy, and scattered particles flying about in Thy shining rays.

O Lord, O Lord, render us successful through Thy conquering power, in that which Thou lovest and approvest, so that we may become standards of guidance, signs of Thy Kingdom, the El-ABHA [and that we may] adore Thee, supplicate before the Kingdom of Thy mercy, beseech Thy realm of might, be submissive to Thy servants, humble before Thy maid-servants, severed from aught else save Thee, sincerely turned unto Thy face, aflame with the fire of Thy love, diffusing thy fragrances, united in Thy Cause, of one accord in Thy religion, and firm in Thy Covenant.

order.why: Establish wisdom and utterance as the requested means of drawing people near.
shortened: O my Lord! Thou seest me walking in Thy dominion to exalt Thy Word, and speaking among Thy servants what Thou hast commanded me in Thy Book. I beseech Thee by the waves of the ocean of Thy grace, and by the Lamp which Thou hast protected from tempestuous winds through the glass of Thy strength and power, to ordain for me that which will make me strong through Thy strength and powerful through Thy will, that I may cast upon Thy servants, with wisdom and utterance, that which will draw them nigh unto Thee and sanctify them from the doubts of the people of Thy earth and the insinuations of those who have denied Thy favor.

order.why: Turn attention from speakers to the needs of hearers.
Connect a traveler’s strength with becoming a source of comfort.
shortened: O Lord! Assist this servant of Thine to spread the fragrances of Thy Covenant and Testament, aid him in Thy remembrance, illumine his face with the light of the star of Thy confirmation, strengthen his back in Thy service, be his companion in his journeys and travels, be his support in all affairs, protect him from the whispers of Satan, open before him the doors of success, overshadow him with clouds of prosperity, make him a source of comfort to souls and a spirit to those hearts which have been revived by the joyous breezes in the world of forms.

order.why: Read the practical need to gather scattered affairs.
Include those who serve and sustain traveling teachers.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the Word through which, when it was raised up in the world, all things spoke and the earth and heaven were stirred, to make me steadfast among Thy servants in service to Thy loved ones who have traversed the lands to propagate Thy Cause and to kindle hearts with the fire of Thy divine Tree.

order.why: Hear the prayer for healing, renewed strength, and life-giving speech.
Read reliance on divine power amid personal lowliness.
Consider thirst, poverty, and weakness as images of receptivity.
Hear the collective longing for guidance and healing.
Read the traveler’s prayer across distance, unfamiliarity, and daily devotion.
shortened: O God, my God! Thou seest me enraptured and attracted toward Thy glorious kingdom, enkindled with the fire of Thy love amongst mankind, a herald of Thy kingdom in these vast and spacious lands, severed from aught else save Thee, relying on Thee, abandoning rest and comfort, remote from my native home, a wanderer in these regions, a stranger fallen upon the ground, humble before Thine exalted threshold, submissive toward the heaven of Thine omnipotent glory, supplicating Thee in the dead of night and at the break of dawn, entreating and invoking Thee at morn and at eventide to graciously aid me to serve Thy Cause, to spread abroad Thy teachings and to exalt Thy Word throughout the East and the West.

order.why: Consider travel from East to West through the capacities and joy of those encountered.
Read the concise petition to strengthen a weak person’s service.
Connect expanded understanding with the easing of affairs.
Hear the wish that earthly and heavenly means be gathered for service.
Read the learned servant’s dependence on an opened door of understanding.
shortened: O my God, my God! I stretch forth my imploring hands toward the Kingdom of might and glory, and I beseech Thee to open before the face of Thy learned servant Thy spacious door, and inspire him with the signs of Thy oneness, the mysteries of Thy singleness, and the manifestations of Thy sanctity. Aid him with the hosts of Thy celestial Kingdom and the armies of Thy mighty dominion.

order.why: Consider the request to learn sciences and mysteries.
shortened: My Lord and my Hope! Aid these souls to acquire the sciences that demonstrate the appearance of Thy Beauty in the realm of creation, and teach them the mysteries that were in the unseen world of contingent being.

order.why: Explore teaching the teachers what they need for service.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the Most Great Word and by the fragrances of Thy raiment amidst the Concourse on high, to teach Thy loved ones that which will enable them to arise to serve Thy Cause and to speak forth Thy praise and glorification.

O Lord! Teach them what Thou hast willed in Thy days and what Thou hast ordained through the Pen of Thy Command, for I am certain that should they become aware of that which Thou hast destined for them in Thy Kingdom, they would soar with longing and yearning in the atmosphere of Thy commandments and would hold fast to that which Thou hast enjoined upon them in Thy Book.

order.why: Read the request for knowledge in teaching young people.
shortened: I rub my face in the dust of Thy luminous threshold, in humility, supplication, imploring, communing and seeking aid, that Thou mayest assist this servant through the inspirations of the unseen realm of Thy mercy and enable him to teach the youth Thy clear and manifest proof and Thy conclusive arguments to all the worlds.

order.why: Connect an expanded heart with explaining proofs and evidence.
Join understanding, glad tidings, healing, and guidance.
shortened: O Lord, O Lord! Grant him and them success, strengthen him and them, inspire him and teach them until they speak forth Thy manifest proofs, Thy clear evidences, and Thy brilliant glad-tidings, quench the thirst, heal the sick, and guide people to the path, O my Glorious Lord!

order.why: Hear the petition for wisdom and lucid speech.
Read the invitation toward knowledge and understanding across religions.
shortened: Enable us to teach Thy Cause with wisdom and utterance throughout the contingent world and to guide the followers of all religions to the city of knowledge and understanding.

order.why: Place wise service within gratitude for having received guidance.
shortened: When thou beholdest the waves of the ocean of the Most Merciful's utterance, say: O Lord of Religions! Praise be unto Thee for having guided me in Thy days, shown me the traces of Thy Pen, made me to know Thy path, the Dawning-Place of Thy mighty signs, and the Dayspring of Thy Revelation and Thy mysteries.

I beseech Thee, O Light of the world, by Thy Most Great Name whereby the hearts of nations were stirred, and by the lands which were honored by Thy footsteps, and by the air wherein Thy call was raised, and by the spot which Thou didst adorn with Thy presence and didst make the Greatest Panorama among mankind, to assist me to serve Thy Cause among Thy servants with wisdom and utterance.

order.why: Consider inner and outer strength through the hosts of wisdom and utterance.
Retain the concise petition naming those same means.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O Lord of existence and Sovereign of the seen and unseen, to assist me to serve Thy Cause through the hosts of wisdom and utterance.

order.why: Read remembrance and praise through wisdom in expression.
shortened: I beseech Thee, by the lights of the dawn of Thy Revelation, to assist me in making mention of Thee and in praising Thee with wisdom and utterance.

order.why: Hear the request for wise utterance among different religions.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O Thou Who rulest over the kingdom of names, by the pearls of wisdom and utterance which lay within the shells of the oceans of Thy knowledge and wisdom, and by the Point through which Thou didst detail Thy Books, to aid me to make mention of Thee with wisdom and utterance and to speak Thy praise amidst all religions.

order.why: Consider wisdom learned from the Tablets as assistance in service.
Connect steadfastness, travel, and wisdom in a single prayer.
shortened: Say: My God, my God! Praise be to Thee for having enabled me to turn to Thee and for revealing to me what was hidden and concealed from the eyes of Thy creatures. I beseech Thee, O Fulfiller of the needs of all seekers, to assist Thy Cause through wisdom and utterance. Strengthen, O my God, Thy loved ones to remain steadfast in Thy love and service. O Lord! Thou seest Thy trusted servant traversing the lands to manifest Thy Cause and exalt Thy Word. Aid him, O my God, with the hosts of revelation and inspiration, and with the angels on high.

order.why: Read the appeal to verses and clear proofs as the means of assistance.
Follow the hoped-for effects of speech on insight, conscience, and the heart.
shortened: Lord, Lord! Breathe into his spirit the breath of the All-Merciful, loose his tongue in the field of remembrance and utterance, inspire him with the verses of guidance among humanity, illuminate through him the inner visions, bring joy to watchful eyes through him, make sweet the thoughts through him, purify the consciences through him, and adorn the inmost hearts through him, so that he may guide the people of error to the path of truth, lead the parched and thirsty to the sweet waters, and perfume the nostrils of the people of enlightenment with a sweet fragrance from the verdant garden and luxuriant grove.

order.why: Read teaching through dispelling sorrow and awakening joy.
shortened: O Lord of the brilliant signs! Illumine the hearts with the lights of Thy love in these days which gleam and shine with the light of the Covenant in the midst of the horizons, that they may guide people to Thy straight path, spread Thy teachings in the most excellent way, diffuse Thy traces throughout those regions, enlighten eyes with the brilliance of lights, delight ears with hearing proof and demonstration, expand breasts with abundant bounty, gladden hearts through the dispelling of sorrows, intoxicate spirits with the wine of joy, and spread traces throughout all lands.

order.why: Consider joyful protection and the flow of understanding to receptive souls.
shortened: Bestow upon him Thy manifold bounties, unravel before him Thy hidden mysteries, and preserve him from every affliction and sorrow, within the stronghold of Thine unfailing protection. O God! Open Thou the gates of joy and happiness for him in this marvellous age, so that the verities of Thy Cause may flow from him in torrents to every ardent and grateful soul. O Lord! Grant that his sole aim, his only goal, may be to diffuse Thy sweet savours amidst humankind and to spread Thy light throughout the world.

order.why: Hear the prayer to quench thirst and heal through service.
Read the teacher as a tree offering refuge and shade.
shortened: O Lord! Assist this unique servant and make him the unique one of the new age and the distinguished individual, that he may quicken the decayed bones through the holy fragrances of Thy sanctity in that distant region. My Lord! Make him a rising star, an articulate tongue, a radiant lamp, and a lofty tree, that all who fear the promised Day and severe chastisement may seek refuge in his shade.

order.why: Consider the unknown servant through water, healing, and guidance.
shortened: O Lord! Make this unknown one renowned throughout all regions through Thy love, and make this nameless one known in East and West through the light of guidance. Place in my hand a brimming cup of the wine of Thy love that I may intoxicate the world with this pure wine and lead the thirsty to the spring of living waters. May I guide the seekers of Thy beauty to the gathering of meeting and direct the sick to the loving Physician.

order.why: Read the many images of fruitful and life-giving influence.
shortened: Guide through them all peoples and nations, O my merciful Lord! Illumine through them the horizons of existence, make them like rain-bearing clouds, transform through them the mirage into cool drink, cause through them the gardens of hearts to grow, make fruitful through them the trees of being, build through them the solid structure, demolish through them the buried foundation, shelter them in Thy prosperous house, establish their names in Thy preserved tablet, and praise them in Thy unfurled scroll.

order.why: Hear joy and knowledge within the imagery of birds and songs.
shortened: O my Lord! Ignite the fire of attraction in their hearts; let the birds of knowledge soar in the rose-gardens of their breasts and sing in the meadows of their souls, songs of love with the most wonderful melodies and harmonies; make them strong verses; unfurled ensigns and perfect words; elevate thy Cause by them; raise thy banners, spread thy signs, assist thy Word and support thy friends by them; make them to utter in thy praise and inspire them to arise in thy good-pleasure; illumine their faces in the Kingdom of thy holiness, and complete their joy by confirming them in assisting thy Cause!

order.why: Consider wings of knowledge, bounty, and grace.
shortened: O Lord, give them wings by the power of divine confirmation that they may soar to heights no person of wisdom can attain. Plant in their wings the brilliant signs of might and power, the shoulders of glory and knowledge, and the primary feathers of bounty and grace, that they may hover at the zenith of guidance and warble the sweetest melodies in the highest Paradise.

order.why: Read speech within gatherings of joy and light.
shortened: Unloose his tongue in Thy praise in the assemblies of light, inspire him with the verses of Thy unity in the gatherings of joy and delight, and diffuse through him the sweet savours of Thy holiness in every land and region.

order.why: Hear the request to contribute remembrance to a gathering of women.
shortened: Let me arise to serve Thy Cause and with most wondrous melodies open my tongue to Thy remembrance in gatherings of the maidservants of the All-Merciful, and adorn the meeting.

order.why: Join explaining the Cause to humility in serving others.
shortened: Confirm me to deliver Thy Cause, enable me to call in Thy Name, and cause me to show forth the proofs of Thy Manifestation. Strengthen me to promote Thy Word, dilate my breast by serving Thy maid-servants and being humble and submissive before Thy beloved ones.

order.why: Consider encouragement that enables a whole community to arise together.
Read collective service through an ocean of oneness.
shortened: Assist us to serve at Thy holy Threshold, enable us to worship Thee at the dawning-places of Thy mention, and ordain for us to spread the sweet fragrances of Thy holiness amongst Thy creation. Strengthen our loins in Thy service amongst Thy servants until we may guide the nations to Thy Most Great Name and lead the peoples to the most noble shore of the sea of Thy oneness.

order.why: Retain the parallel communal petition in its own wording.
shortened: Enable us to diffuse Thy holy fragrances amongst Thy creatures, and strengthen our loins to serve Thee amidst Thy servants, so that we may guide all nations to Thy Most Great Name and lead all peoples to the shores of the glorious ocean of Thy oneness.

order.why: Hear the request to gather believers beneath a shared light.
shortened: O my God, O thou who quickenest the hearts with the fragrance of the Covenant, O thou who dost illumine the eyes! Assist thy humble servant, submissive at the door of thy oneness, that he may raise up thy Word in these remote region, that he may spread abroad Thy fragrance in Thy Path, and gather together the believers beneath the sheltering beams of Thy perspicuous light and dilate their breasts with the manifestation of thy assistance from the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Consider the gathering of souls beneath a banner of mercy.
Read collective strength for teaching in many directions.
shortened: Through them exalt Thy Word among humanity and spread through them the fragrances of Thy oneness in those regions. Strengthen them with Thy power that prevails over all things, and gird up their loins to arise to spread Thy teachings in all directions.

order.why: Hear the wish that remembrance spread through all regions.
Read the expansive devotional imagery of certitude, light, and love.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the cries of the hearts of Thy chosen ones, and by the flames of fire blazing within the ribs and bowels of Thy loved ones, and by the flowing tears from the eyes of those who long for Thee, and by the burning embers in the hearts of those who are in love with Thee, to raise up the roaring of the lions of divine knowledge in the thickets of the seat of Thy manifestation, and cause the whales of certitude to swim in the pools from which flowed the waters of Thy bounty on the day of Thy dawning, and kindle the fires of Thy love in those regions, and illuminate those precincts with lights that shine between earth and heaven, and perfume those areas with the sweet fragrances of Thy holiness, O Thou Who possessest the Most Beautiful Names!

order.why: Keep the martial metaphors directed toward hearts and spirits through holy fragrances.
shortened: My God, my God! These are souls at peace in Thy remembrance, content with Thy decree, well-pleased in Thy holy court. Assist them with the hosts arrayed in the Supreme Concourse and the reinforced armies from Thy Abha Kingdom. Make their tongues as spearheads raised in Thy remembrance and as drawn swords in teaching Thy Cause, that they may conquer the citadels of hearts and spirits through the fragrances of Thy holiness. Verily Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful, the Self-Subsisting Lord. Verily Thou art the Bestower, the All-Bountiful.

order.why: Read conquest within the prayer’s stated aim of guidance and revival.
Consider the requested firmness of the Covenant amid commotion.
shortened: O Lord! Assist Thy servant whom Thou hast chosen for the promotion of Thy Cause and the diffusion of the fragrance of Thy sanctification and the manifestation of the signs of Thy oneness. O Lord! Strengthen his back and gird up his loins and make his affairs easy and illumine his face and loose his tongue that he may make Thy servants firm in Thy Covenant and Testament and become a mighty barrier of iron between Thy servants and Gog of commotion and Magog of upheaval.

order.why: Retain the polemical personal petition as its source’s voice, not a general model of addressing others.
shortened: As for the matter of that sinful son of sin, that brutal outcast - may God bind his fate to his neck and bring forth for him an unfurled book from Sijjin - I beseech God to assist thee in writing the response and to expand thy breast with the light of knowledge and to strengthen thy pen with confirmation from the Supreme Pen, so that the response may be an explanation of the complex issues in this matter, thus driving away the followers of that doubting barker.

order.why: Hear the request for protection and continuing assistance.
shortened: O learned one who understands the mysteries! I beseech the Mighty, the All-Choosing One, and I supplicate night and day, and I pray for confirmation and success for you among the righteous ones, and for assistance and protection from evil ones.

order.why: Read protection from oppression together with awakening through utterance.
shortened: O my God, my Lord and my Hope! I beseech Thee by the cry of them that are nigh unto Thee, by the lamentation of the sincere ones, by the yearning of the lovers, and by the exultation of them that know Thee in Thy love, to preserve him whom Thou hast aided to turn towards Thee and whom Thou hast caused to enter the pavilion of majesty and given to drink from the fountain of bounty and grace. Protect him beneath Thy sheltering care from the oppression of Thy creatures, and grant him always the blessing of Thy tender mercies and the pure waters of Thy loving-kindness.

Exalt his station in service to Thy Cause and aid him to teach Thy Faith throughout Thy lands in such wise that through his utterance the ready ones may be guided, the seated ones may arise, and the slumbering ones may be awakened.

order.why: Keep the aged servant’s suffering and yearning in its devotional context.
Retain the particular petition concerning the unique martyr.
shortened: O Lord! Assist Thy servant, the unique martyr, to spread Thy beautiful remembrance in every far-reaching region, and exalt through him Thy Word, and diffuse through him Thy teachings, and manifest through him Thy signs among the righteous ones.

order.why: Consider steadfast service before the power of princes.
shortened: I beseech Thee to assist me to aid Thy Cause among Thy creatures in such wise that the power of princes shall not weaken me.

order.why: Read the Manifestation’s petition in its distinctive first-person station.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy Name through which Thou hast made me the Qayyum over all names and the Manifestation of Thy signs between earth and heaven, to make me a servant unto Thyself, one who speaks in Thy remembrance, stands firm in Thy Cause, wields power over Thy servants, and holds sway over those in Thy earth and Thy heaven, that I may remain steadfast in manifesting Thy Cause in such wise that the turning away of Thy servants and the cawing of Thy creatures shall not deter me.

order.why: Hear the prayer for confirmation and the breath of the Spirit.
Consider service joined to love and nearness.
Read servitude as the setting for attracting hearts.
shortened: Lord! Assist them to serve Thy Cause, enable them in servitude at Thy Threshold, spread through them Thy signs throughout all regions, and through them attract hearts overflowing with the wine of mysteries.

order.why: Hear the desire to serve, praise, and draw near.
Return to attentiveness and detachment.
shortened: Turn thy face toward the holy court and say: O my God and my Beloved! Deprive me not in these days of the breezes of Thy mercy and the melodies of the Dove of Thy gracious favors. Make me ever looking toward Thee and detached from all else besides Thee.

order.why: Read the movement from receiving the Word to arising in service.
Consider the speaker’s continued need to drink from knowledge and utterance.
shortened: Then cause me to drink, at all times, from the Salsabil of Thy knowledge and the Kawthar of Thy utterance, whereby the hearts of Thy servants and the souls of Thy creatures may be drawn.

order.why: Read the strengthening of will through remembrance.
shortened: Let their hearts, O my Lord, be carried away by Thy remembrance, and their souls enriched by Thy riches, and their wills strengthened to proclaim Thy Cause amidst Thy creatures.

order.why: Connect service with detachment and evidence in one’s life.
Hear the request that conduct be worthy of the Cause.
Bring speech beside acting according to the Book.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy arising to promote the Cause and Thy exalting the word of justice, and by Thy most great signs at whose descent all things proclaimed sovereignty and dominion, might and power unto Thy most exalted Self and Thy most glorious Name, to make me one who speaketh of Thy remembrance, who gazeth toward Thy horizon, and who acteth according to that which Thou hast commanded me in Thy Book.

order.why: Consider service through doing what is loved and approved.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the heaven of Thy grace and the sea of Thy power and the sun of Thy Cause to assist me in serving Thee and in praising Thee amongst Thy servants, and to enable me to do that which Thou lovest and art pleased with.

order.why: Read holding fast to guidance before guiding others.
shortened: O Lord! Aid us to hold fast unto Thee and unto that which hath been sent down from Thee, and assist this Thy servant to guide Thy creatures and direct them to Thy path.

order.why: Hear the prayer to lead toward oneness and detachment.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the Most Great Name to assist me to serve Thy Cause that I may guide the servants to the shore of the ocean of Thy oneness and bring them nigh unto the Dawning-Place of detachment through Thy Name and Thy sovereignty.

order.why: Connect remembrance with continual nearness.
Retain the petition for assistance with its source omission.
Consider an enduring good remembrance through service.
shortened: O my Lord! Aid me in Thy days to serve Thy Cause, that I may thereby possess the mention of good throughout the perpetuity of Thy names and attributes.

order.why: Hear the prayer that the Book’s teachings become manifest through a person.
Retain the concise petition for remembrance to spread.
Read proclamation together with the requested gift of nearness.
shortened: Make them able, moreover, to proclaim Thy name amidst Thy creatures, and supply them with the best of what Thou hast destined for such of Thy chosen ones as enjoy near access to Thee.

order.why: Consider attraction through the speaker’s remembrance.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O Cleaver of the Dawn and Sender of the Winds, to assist me to serve Thy Cause in such wise that through my mention the hearts of Thy servants and the souls of Thy creatures may be attracted.

order.why: Keep the particular prayer for Javad and its awakening imagery.
Hear the servant’s request to arise and call.
Retain the brief prayer for strengthened service.
shortened: This is a servant who hath been attracted by the fragrances of Thy holiness, and enkindled with the fire of Thy love, and hath spoken in Thy praise, and witnessed Thy signs, and searched through Thy words, and pondered Thy evidences, and been gladdened by Thy glad-tidings. O Lord! Make him a fragrance from the gardens of Thy oneness, and a breeze from the direction of Thy grace, and a tree from the groves of Thy bounty, and a bird from the gardens of Thy mercy, and a flower from the bower of Thy loving-kindness. O Lord! Strengthen him to serve Thee and spread Thy traces and exalt Thy Cause.

order.why: Read the shared petition to remember, praise, and serve.
A prayer for assistance in teaching, serving and proclaiming divine favors.
Consider communicating a path through its signs.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the ocean of Thy bounty and the heaven of Thy giving to make me speak forth among Thy creation that I may acquaint them with Thy straight Path and Thy mighty Message, and show them Thy signs and the manifestations of Thy power.

order.why: Hear the prayer for remembrance in every circumstance.
shortened: Say: O God of the world and Goal of the nations! I beseech Thee by the Light whereby the heavens of utterance were illumined for all contingent beings, and by the Fire whereby the Tree of Knowledge was set ablaze, to enable me in all circumstances and times to remember Thee, to praise Thee, and to serve Thy Cause in this Day wherein the hidden Secret and the treasured Symbol that hath spoken and doth speak "Verily there is no God but Me, the Almighty, the Powerful" hath been made manifest.

order.why: Connect speaking a name with continued attention to its source.
shortened: Say: My God, my God! I beseech Thee by the light of Thy Cause that shineth forth and by that which lay hidden in the treasuries of Thy power, to ordain for me that which shall cause me to speak forth Thy name in Thy lands and to gaze upon Thy horizon.

order.why: Read the collective desire to arise in service.
shortened: We beseech Thee, O Creator of the heavens and Lord of all names, by the Most Great Word which hath proceeded from the mouth of Thy Will and the Pen of Thy Purpose, to assist us in remembering and praising Thee and in arising to serve Thy Cause.

order.why: Consider an opened heart as a hoped-for result.
shortened: O Lord! Thou seest him who hath turned toward Thee - make him then to arise to serve Thy Cause, to speak Thy praise, and to open the hearts of Thy servants through Thy Name.

order.why: Join the spread of knowledge with firmness.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O Lord of Names, by Thy Name which hath dominion over earth and heaven, to assist them to spread Thy knowledge amongst Thy creation and to stand firm in Thy Cause within Thy realm.

order.why: Hear remembrance and teaching within one concise request.
shortened: O my Lord! Aid me in Thy remembrance and praise and in teaching Thy Cause and in that whereby Thy Most Exalted Word may be upraised in the world of creation.

order.why: Read the prayer for generosity toward one devoted to service.
shortened: Moreover I beseech Thee, O Thou Sovereign of bounty and Lord of the Kingdom of Names, by Thy most sweet call and by the signs of Thy power in the kingdom of creation, to rain down from the heaven of Thy grace upon him who hath confined his affairs to Thy mention and praise amongst Thy servants and who hath arisen to serve Thy Cause, the rain-showers of Thy generosity, the gentle drops of Thy munificence and the outpourings of Thy favors.

order.why: Return to guidance and love as the ends of the undertaking.
Close with the person who is old in faith and young in love.

questions: How does the desire to be taught change the way someone might teach?
What do the images of the broken-winged bird, thirst, and weakness reveal about spiritual confidence?
How might wisdom and clear utterance require attention to the hearer as well as the speaker?
What does Moses’s prayer in Qur’an 20:25–28 suggest about the relationship between inward preparation and being understood?
How could practical support, care for health, and service to fellow workers form part of a teaching effort?
What signs would show that sharing a conviction has brought greater understanding, comfort, or unity?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 20:25–28 · Moses asks for ease and intelligible speech
references.note: Read Pickthall’s translation of verses 25–28, using the linked verse numbers to continue through Moses’s request. Compare the petitions for relief, ease in the task, and words that can be understood with the compilation’s prayers for expanded capacity and wise utterance. What preparation concerns the speaker, and what is sought for those who listen?

subjects.displayTitle: Divine freedom: independence, generosity, and the limits of understanding
subjects.introduction: Nothing we do reaches God. Our obedience, the Báb says in prayer, adds nothing to Him, and the remoteness of those who turn away takes nothing from the treasuries of His grandeur. Such independence might seem to leave worship without a point, yet Bahá’u’lláh insists that this self-sufficient God has had no purpose save the guidance of His servants, that He turns His face toward us and calls, though He never needed anything that was or shall be. The Báb’s litanies press the thought to its edge, heaping up names and negations until language confesses its limits: a nearness closer than the life-vein which, seen from His height, is still the distance between heaven and earth. Paul’s word in Athens about a God who needs nothing from human hands, yet gives all life and breath and is not far from any of us, holds the same two truths together [1]. The path continues into transcendence and unknowability, the power and sovereignty of God, and the mystery of suffering.
subjects.arc: Begin with guidance freely given by a God beyond need, explore created dependence and the limits of praise, then consider sovereign revelation, prayer, and the supplied philosophical arguments.

order.why: Read the reported account of absolute freedom and renewed subsidiary laws.
shortened: There is a divine freedom, and this is peculiar unto the Essence of the Creator; for He is absolutely free. In no respect, nor in any of His modes or attributes, can any soul constrain Him. By His sovereign and unrestricted Will, in every age the sacred laws have been renewed, and the subsidiary ordinances, according to the exigencies of each time, have been changed.

order.why: Open with guidance as the purpose of One beyond gain or harm.
shortened: He hath had and hath no purpose save the guidance of the handmaidens and servants of God, inasmuch as He, of His own Self, hath ever been and shall ever be self-sufficient. Neither doth any good deed of His servants profit Him, nor any evil act of His creatures harm Him.

order.why: Consider the gift of being called despite divine self-sufficiency.
shortened: Thou, verily, render thanks unto God for that the Countenance of the Ancient of Days hath turned toward thee from this praised station, and calleth thee unto Him, though He was self-sufficient above whatsoever hath appeared in what was and shall be.

order.why: Read independence from both acceptance and rejection.
shortened: O servant! Bear thou witness, as God did witness before the creation of the heavens and the earth and before He created the glorifying angels, that He is the One God, Single, Self-Sufficient, Whom the support of those who turn unto Him cannot exalt nor the rejection of those who turn away from Him harm, and that Ali is His splendor and His light unto all created things.

order.why: Hear the Bab’s statement that obedience adds nothing to God.
Extend independence beyond human deeds to political power.
shortened: Thou, verily, art He Whom the good works of the people can never exalt nor their evil deeds deter, Whom the ascendancy of the rulers cannot humble nor the power of the mighty vanquish. Thou doest through Thy sovereignty whatsoever Thou willest.

order.why: Establish the contrast between divine independence and created dependence.
shortened: When thou hast recognized thy Lord God through His independence of what He hath created and will create, and the dependence of what He hath created and will create upon His command, then bear thou witness that God, glorified be He, hath no beginning and no end, no outward and no inward.

order.why: Consider even human praise as enabled by divine power.
shortened: Thou hast, in Thyself, been independent of any one besides Thee and rich enough, in Thine own essence, to dispense with any one except Thy Self. Every description by which they who adore Thy unity describe Thee, and every praise wherewith they who are devoted unto Thee praise Thee, are but the traces of the pen which the fingers of Thy strength and power have set in motion -- fingers whose movement is controlled by the arm of Thy decree -- the arm itself animated by the potency of Thy might.

order.why: Explore the limits of knowledge, praise, and conceptions of nearness.
shortened: Thou hast never been and will never be known as Thou deservest to be known, nor worshipped as Thou deservest to be worshipped, nor described by what Thou hast created in existence, nor characterized by what Thou hast brought into being in the realities of contingent things. For Thy Reality, as it is in itself, severs all created things from the paths of knowledge and recognition, and Thy pure Essence, as it is in itself, separates all existent things from mention of nearness and expression.

The mention of Thy nearness being closer than the life-vein, in the eyes of them that gaze upon Thy loftiness and exaltation, is naught but as the distance between heaven and earth. Glorified art Thou! Glorified art Thou! This is according to my measure, as revealed in Thy Book, else Thou art He Whose nearness none can know but Thee, and Whose remoteness none can fathom but Thee.

order.why: Read the negation of spatial and directional descriptions.
shortened: Thou art He Who is not of anything, nor in anything, nor upon anything, nor before anything, nor after anything, nor above anything, nor below anything, nor to the right of anything, nor to the left of anything, nor in any direction of anything.

order.why: Consider the limits of association and rational comprehension.
shortened: In the eternity of Thy essence, Thou wert sanctified from association with contingent things, and the oneness of Thy being was hallowed from the reach of the perceptions of those endowed with reason.

order.why: Hear the prayer’s reflection on the very language used to address God.
Read the extended names, oneness, and transcendence of the Book of Names.
shortened: Thou hast ever been One God, Single, Eternal, Individual, Ever-living, Self-subsisting, Sovereign, Supreme, Holy, Everlasting, Eternal, Self-dependent, Transcendent, Inaccessible, inasmuch as Thou hast taken unto Thyself neither consort nor son, and there hath been no partner for Thee in what Thou hast created, nor any helper in what Thou hast fashioned.

Exalted is God above all that they attribute unto Him, before and after! All that is in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them glorify Him, and all that is in the kingdom of command and creation and whatsoever is beneath them bow down before Him. There is none other God but He, the All-Compelling, the Self-Subsisting.

order.why: Consider the rejection of peers, opposites, and likenesses.
Hear the prayer’s affirmation of enduring self-sufficiency.
shortened: Thou hast taken unto Thyself neither peer nor partner nor helper, and Thou wilt ever be as Thou hast been from all eternity. There is no God but Thee, the Self-Sufficient, the Most Exalted.

order.why: Read the Bab’s names and the denial of a helper in creation.
shortened: Thou hast ever been one God, single, eternal, self-subsisting, living, enduring, sovereign, all-pervading, holy, everlasting, forever, inaccessible, possessing, ruling, manifest, powerful. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast no partner in what Thou hast created, nor any helper in what Thou hast fashioned.

order.why: Consider living being beyond creaturely generation.
shortened: Thou hast taken neither consort nor partner, nor hath anything in Thy realm been joined with Thy Being, for Thou wert living when there was no life, and Thou wilt live after all life, and Thou art living when there is no life except Thine own. Thou createst what Thou willest without generation, and bringest into being what Thou desirest without invention.

order.why: Read origination without peer or partner.
shortened: Thou hast ever existed before all things, and Thou wilt forever remain before all things. Thou createst what Thou willest through Thy creation and Thou bringest into being what Thou desirest through Thy origination. Thou hast no equal, no likeness, no similitude, no peer and no partner. Thou createst what Thou willest through Thy creation and Thou originatest what Thou desirest through Thy innovation.

order.why: Explore the asymmetry of creator and created through paired affirmations.
Hear the relation of creative command to transcendence before, with, and after things.
Read the measured order of creation through will and decree.
shortened: Glorified art Thou, O God! I and all things bear witness that Thou hast ever been One God, Single, Alone, Eternal, Self-Subsisting, the All-Wise, the Just, the Holy, the Everlasting, the Eternal, the Self-Dependent. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast had no partner in sovereignty, nor any protector in all the earth save by Thy leave. Thou didst ordain the creation of all things and fashion them according to Thy Will, and Thou didst determine the measures of all things by Thy leave and decree them by Thy ordering.

order.why: Consider sovereignty without a need for possession.
Read power together with wisdom and transcendence.
Retain the concise affirmation of creation without partner or helper.
shortened: Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast no partner in what Thou hast created, nor any helper in what Thou hast fashioned.

order.why: Hear independence of what has been and will be created.
Affirms God’s independence of possessions while calling for service and assistance.
Consider transcendence even above what has been revealed.
shortened: Exalted is God, thy Lord and the Lord of all things, above whatsoever hath been sent down and shall be sent down.

order.why: Read the prayer’s pairing of power, decree, will, and wisdom.
shortened: Thou hast taken neither consort nor offspring, nor hast Thou had any partner in Thy creation or any protector in what Thou hast fashioned. By Thy power hast Thou created all things and ordained them according to Thy decree, and by Thy will hast Thou formed the creation of all things and shaped them according to Thy wisdom.

order.why: Hear all things bearing witness to self-subsistence.
Retain this distinct prayer’s formulation of independence.
Read the sequence of creating, ordaining, forming, and fashioning.
Consider the ordered world through wisdom and will.
shortened: Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, nor hath there been any partner in what Thou hast created, nor any protector in what Thou hast fashioned. By Thy wisdom hast Thou ordered the kingdom of Thy heaven and earth, and by Thy will hast Thou perfected the affairs of all in the kingdom of Thy Cause and creation.

order.why: Hear the varied divine names without reducing them to one human category.
Retain the separate affirmation of eternal, inaccessible life.
Read the prayer’s concise account of oneness and the ordaining of things.
shortened: Thou hast ever been one God, single, unique, eternal, self-subsisting. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, nor hast Thou manifested this through any of Thy creation, and Thou hast ordained all things by Thy power.

order.why: Consider the names that join manifestation and hiddenness.
Hear justice and holiness within the affirmation of self-subsistence.
shortened: Thou hast ever been One, Self-subsistent, Peerless, Living, Eternal, Just, Holy, Abiding, Everlasting, Self-dependent, and All-Glorious. Thou hast taken unto Thyself neither consort nor son.

order.why: Read the intense devotional language of independence even of the Self.
Consider what created existence possesses through dependence alone.
shortened: Hath any power apart from Thee, O my God? Hath any independence save through Thee? Is there for aught beside Thee a sign or proof of self-subsistence? Nay, by Thy might! All are upheld by Thee and by Thy power; and whatever is ascribed unto Thee they know only by themselves upon the earth. But should the relation unto Thee be severed from their souls, they possess nothing; and though they be not true in their claim to Thee, never dost Thou, O my God, confirm their claim unto Thyself.

order.why: Read worship and neglect as unable to alter God, preserving the source gap.
Hear detachment and divine gifts alongside absolute independence.
shortened: Thou dost shower in every state the wonderful tokens of Thy Lordship upon him who hath detached himself unto Thee in his inmost essence, and Thou wilt ever manifest the signs of Thy mighty Self-Subsistence unto him who seeth naught but Thee save as in the day of his nothingness and desireth none but Thee. For Thou hast ever been independent of all that Thou hast created or wilt create, sanctified above all that Thou hast brought into being or wilt bring into being, exalted above all that Thou hast fashioned or wilt fashion, and transcendent above all that Thou hast ordained or wilt ordain.

order.why: Retain the reported statement of divine immutability.
Read the reported claim that creation adds nothing to divine being.
Keep the reported account of creation and other religions attributed.
shortened: All the founders of religion, from Zoroaster and Buddha down to the Bab and Baha'u'llah teach, however, that God has created the world, or, that He has emanated it, that is, let it flow out of Himself, from which derives that God is eternal, the world however temporal.

order.why: Read the reported contrast with philosophers as a particular philosophical characterization.
shortened: Their difference with the Prophets is only in this: that the Prophets say that universal reality and all-encompassing aspect is the absolutely wealthy, perceiving and choosing by will, while the philosophers consider it poor, non-perceiving and powerless.

order.why: Consider grace, justice, and bounty in the Bab’s account.
Read the extended Book of Reckoning passages through command, creation, guidance, and mercy.
shortened: Say: God through His Own Self is independent of His Own Self, for He is the Mighty, the Beloved. Say: God through His Own Essence is independent of His Own Essence, for He is the All-Compelling, the All-Holy. Say: God through His Own Being is independent of His Own Being, for He is the Inaccessible, the Most High, the Mighty, the Beloved. Say: God through His Own Identity is independent of His Own Identity, for He is the Single, the One, the Unique, the Self-Subsisting, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting.

And unto God belong the circles of mercy, which He showereth upon whomsoever He willeth amongst His servants. Verily, He is the preserver of all things. And unto God belongeth all command, both before and after. He createth what He willeth through His command, and God is nigh unto all things.

order.why: Hear the City of Unity’s statement of sovereign will.
Read the seal’s concentrated affirmation of sovereignty.
Consider the granting and withholding described in the commentary.
Retain the concise prayer affirming divine power and ordinance.
shortened: Thou hast power to do what Thou willest, and Thou ordainest what Thou pleasest.

order.why: Hear the parallel formulation concerning creation and will.
Preserve the litany’s repeated wording and source repetition markers.
Read the image of all reins held within divine power.
Hear eternal oneness and unconstrained power together.
shortened: He hath ever been One from all eternity and powerful over whatsoever He willeth.
Verily Thou art powerful over what Thou willest.

order.why: Consider command in the hands of God.
shortened: The Command is in God's hands. He doeth what He willeth and ordaineth what He pleaseth. And He is the Single, the One, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.

order.why: Read the concise assertion that divine action is beyond questioning.
shortened: He is the One Who standeth supreme over His Cause, doing as He willeth, and none can question His doings.

order.why: Consider the sovereignty proclaimed through a divine Name.
Hear independence from opposition and doubt.
shortened: Thou art He Whom the doubts of the heedless and the signs of the opposers cannot hinder. Thou doest what Thou willest and ordainest what Thou pleasest.

order.why: Read the related affirmation concerning human allusions and power.
shortened: Thou art He Whom the doubts of the people have not withheld, nor their allusions, nor their might and power from Thy will and purpose. Through Thee the banner 'He doeth what He willeth and ordaineth what He pleaseth' was raised.

order.why: Consider the challenge to affirming sovereignty while resisting its expression.
shortened: They acknowledge that "He doeth what He willeth," yet they question His actions with "why" and "wherefore." They recognize that "He ordaineth what He pleaseth," yet they hesitate regarding that which hath appeared from Him.

order.why: Read the statement about heaven and earth in its context of recognizing revelation.
shortened: I speak truly when I say that He, exalted be His glory, hath appeared with the banner of 'He doeth what He willeth' and hath come with the standard of 'He ordaineth what He pleaseth.' Let steadfast and content souls be attentive. O My loved ones! Whatsoever proceedeth from the Most Holy, Most Exalted Threshold is the truth about which there is no doubt. The Primal Point hath said that should He pronounce the earth to be heaven or heaven to be earth, none hath the right to question wherefore or why.

order.why: Keep the challenging good-and-evil formulation in its source’s theological voice.
Read the corresponding light-and-darkness formulation without transferring its claim to human authority.
Consider the text’s challenge to objections arising from self and passion.
Keep the polemical scriptural citation attributed within its declaration of freedom.
Read the Bab’s distinct first-person declaration of an enduring light.
Hear the invitation to enter the ocean of oneness.
Consider the account of the true Beloved as the goal of seeking.
Read wisdom and utterance as wings for an answering ascent.
shortened: Thus have We adorned thee with the two wings of wisdom and utterance that thou mayest soar therewith unto the Mighty, the Bestower.

order.why: Hear protection beside possession of all treasures.
shortened: All the kingdoms of heaven and earth and whatever is between them are God's, and His power is supreme over all things. All the treasures of earth and heaven and everything between them are His, and His protection extendeth over all things.

order.why: Read the prayer’s assurance of divine sufficiency.
Consider the limits of created power and knowledge.
shortened: O my God! Thou art sufficient against everyone but none sufficeth against Thee. Verily Thou hast power over all things but all are powerless over anything. Verily Thou knowest all things but all are ignorant of all things.

order.why: Hear the dependent person’s request for shelter and direction.
shortened: Be Thou my supporter behind all things and my shelter with all things. Direct through the sovereignty of Thy direction my affairs, and dispose through the dominion of Thy decree my condition, for besides Thee none hath power over anything, and all else besides Thee is needy and cannot accomplish anything.

order.why: Read sovereign possession through the freedom to bestow mercy.
Close the linked readings with a petition that rests on grace.
Added when a passage was added to a subject compilation.
Read the supplied distinction between the divine Essence and the Primal Utterance.
shortened: Concerning thy question about the meaning of the philosopher's saying, "From the One proceedeth only One": The statement is incorrect when the Cause is meant to be the Absolute Essence... However, when the intention behind the statement is to refer to the Primal Utterance, which is created by God by Itself, for Itself, then verily it is the truth...

There is no doubt that the Eternal Essence hath ever been immeasurably exalted above any association with His creatures; how much less could it become the source out of which things proceed. Though the statement is discussed in philosophy, the truth is that it must refer to the grades of the creative Action itself.

order.why: Consider the supplied objection to locating created forms in the Essence.
shortened: The statement of the philosophers that the cause of the created beings is the Essence is erroneous because of the lack of association [between cause and effect], the utter impossibility of change, and the precondition of the resemblance of the cause and the effect. The truth is that the Cause of beings is God's Handiwork, created by God Himself for Himself, and ordained to be the Cause of all His creation.

order.why: Retain the supplied fragment about causation with its visible source boundaries.
Keep the supplied polemic concerning unity of existence in its own philosophical voice.
End with the supplied account of the Will as created cause, preserving its provisional status.
shortened: Verily God hath intended by these exalted words to sanctify His Essence utterly from any attribute of causation, refuting the views of those who have considered the Essence to be the Cause of all causes.
He hath fashioned the Will from nothingness, through Itself, and ordained It to be the Cause of all that is other than It, with no descent of anything from His Essence unto the Will.

questions: If human deeds neither enrich nor diminish God, whom do worship and obedience benefit?
How do divine independence and freely given guidance illuminate one another in the opening passages?
What do the many names and negations reveal, and where do they mark the limits of human language?
How does Acts 17:24–28 hold together divine freedom from need and nearness to every person?
What questions arise when expectations about revelation meet the claim of an unconstrained divine will?
How might the distinction between the divine Essence, creative action, and created dependence affect the way one prays or confronts suffering?

references.label: 1 · Acts 17:24–28 · The giver of life who needs nothing
references.note: Read the King James Version’s account of God as creator, giver of life, and near to every person. Compare its rejection of the idea that God needs human provision with the compilation’s insistence that worship does not increase divine being. Consider how each account joins dependence with the possibility of seeking and nearness, while retaining its own theological language.

subjects.displayTitle: The laws of God: love, protection, and the practice of faith
subjects.introduction: Observe My commandments, Bahá’u’lláh says, for the love of My beauty: the law is given in the voice of a lover, and its fragrance, He says, can be smelled from His garment. Here they begin with joy, forbidding whatever saddens hearts, and they end in protection: a fortress for the world, a father’s rod of wisdom, a dispensary holding a remedy for every ailment. The Kitáb-i-Aqdas sets two duties side by side, recognising the One who reveals the law and observing what He ordains, and declares them inseparable. From there the questions become concrete: honesty in sustenance, respect for a neighbour’s house and property, the end of holy war, provision for a spouse during a long absence, the Huqúqu’lláh offered freely. Each ruling carries its own history of interpretation and application. The psalmist who begs to understand the statutes so that he may keep them with his whole heart asks for the same delight [1]. The path continues through the twin duties of recognition and obedience, the laws of prayer and fasting, and the law of Huqúqu’lláh.
subjects.arc: Begin with joy and protection as purposes of law, read recognition beside conduct, then explore authority, historical application, particular rulings, and the inward work of observance.

order.why: Read law through the explicit purposes of preservation, comfort, education, and advancement.
Open with the aim of bringing joy to hearts.
Ground the inquiry in recognition, love, protection, and the Kitab-i-Aqdas.
shortened: The first duty prescribed by God for His servants is the recognition of Him Who is the Dayspring of His Revelation and the Fountain of His laws, Who representeth the Godhead in both the Kingdom of His Cause and the world of creation. Whoso achieveth this duty hath attained unto all good; and whoso is deprived thereof hath gone astray, though he be the author of every righteous deed. It behoveth every one who reacheth this most sublime station, this summit of transcendent glory, to observe every ordinance of Him Who is the Desire of the world. These twin duties are inseparable. Neither is acceptable without the other.
The Tongue of My power hath, from the heaven of My omnipotent glory, addressed to My creation these words: "Observe My commandments, for the love of My beauty."

order.why: Bring professed belief to the test of deeds.
shortened: O ye two well-loved handmaids of God! Whatever a man's tongue speaketh, that let him prove by his deeds. If he claimeth to be a believer, then let him act in accordance with the precepts of the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Consider the character by which a community’s faith becomes recognizable.
shortened: Should any one of you enter a city, he should become a centre of attraction by reason of his sincerity, his faithfulness and love, his honesty and fidelity, his truthfulness and loving-kindness towards all the peoples of the world, so that the people of that city may cry out and say: 'This man is unquestionably a Baha'i, for his manners, his behaviour, his conduct, his morals, his nature, and disposition reflect the attributes of the Baha'is.' Not until ye attain this station can ye be said to have been faithful to the Covenant and Testament of God.

order.why: Read respect for homes and possessions as concrete obligations.
shortened: Say: O people! Spread not corruption in the land, and enter not houses save by permission. This is that which ye have been commanded in the Tablets. He, verily, is witness over all things. Beware lest ye wrongfully consume the substance of others.

order.why: Consider the prohibitions on holy war, destruction of books, and seizure of property.
Hear the call toward safety, love, fellowship, and peace.
shortened: The Faith of the Blessed Beauty is summoning mankind to safety and love, to amity and peace; it hath raised up its tabernacle on the heights of the earth, and directeth its call to all nations. Wherefore, O ye who are God's lovers, know ye the value of this precious Faith, obey its teachings, walk in this road that is drawn straight, and show ye this way to the people.

order.why: Read observance through its hoped-for healing effect on others.
shortened: If in this day a soul shall act according to the precepts and the counsels of God, he will serve as a divine physician to mankind, and like the trump of Israfil, he will call the dead of this contingent world to life; for the confirmations of the Abha Realm are never interrupted, and such a virtuous soul hath, to befriend him, the unfailing help of the Company on high. Thus shall a sorry gnat become an eagle in the fulness of his strength, and a feeble sparrow change to a royal falcon in the heights of ancient glory.

order.why: Consider religion’s relation to spiritual and material civilization.
shortened: Religion is the light of the world, and the progress, achievement, and happiness of man result from obedience to the laws set down in the holy Books. Briefly, it is demonstrable that in this life, both outwardly and inwardly the mightiest of structures, the most solidly established, the most enduring, standing guard over the world, assuring both the spiritual and the material perfections of mankind, and protecting the happiness and the civilization of society -- is religion.

order.why: Read ordinances through the image of a protective stronghold.
shortened: They that immerse themselves in the ocean of His utterances should at all times have the utmost regard for the divinely-revealed ordinances and prohibitions. Indeed His ordinances constitute the mightiest stronghold for the protection of the world and the safeguarding of its peoples--a light upon those who acknowledge and recognize the truth, and a fire unto such as turn away and deny.

order.why: Hear the related fortress image while preserving the source omission.
Consider the sweetness and benefit ascribed to commandments.
shortened: Then grant them the sweetness of Thy commandments and Thy laws. Know thou with certainty that Thou dost not command anyone save that which benefits him in all the worlds of Thy creation.

order.why: Explore the account of broad principles within concise scriptural counsels.
shortened: If man observes the divine verses with the eye of fairness and reflects, he will find each passage to be the dawning-place of laws. Reflect upon this blessed verse wherein He says: "Accept thou what is easy, and enjoin what is just, and turn away from the ignorant." And likewise He says: "Be generous as God has been generous to thee." All laws and principles that are the cause of the world's order and the nations' tranquility can be deduced and derived from these two blessed verses.

order.why: Read love of beauty alongside caution against deeds that provoke hatred.
Connect reading, reflection, and action across several named works.
shortened: Through the power of faith, obey ye the teachings of God, and let all your actions conform to His laws. Read ye The Hidden Words, ponder the inner meanings thereof, act in accord therewith. Read, with close attention, the Tablets of Tarazat (Ornaments), Kalimat (Words of Paradise), Tajalliyyat (Effulgences), Ishraqat (Splendours), and Bisharat (Glad Tidings), and rise up as ye are bidden in the heavenly teachings. Thus may each one of you be even as a candle casting its light, the centre of attraction wherever people come together; and from you, as from a bed of flowers, may sweet scents be shed.

order.why: Bring the mystical journey into relation with observance.
shortened: 85 In all these journeys the wayfarer must stray not a hair's breadth from the Law, for this is indeed the secret of the Path and the fruit of the Tree of Truth. And in all these stages he must cling to the robe of obedience to all that hath been enjoined, and hold fast to the cord of shunning all that is forbidden, that he may partake of the cup of the Law and be informed of the mysteries of Truth.

order.why: Consider the reported freeing of a person from destructive habits.
Keep the reported argument from essential relationships in its philosophical setting.
Read the reported physician analogy as an account of changing spiritual prescriptions.
Hear the reported dispensary image as a related account of remedy.
shortened: The divine laws and religions are God's dispensary. The remedy for every ailment exists therein. A skilled physician is needed to apply this cure, one who knows when to use these remedies.

order.why: Keep the reported summary of laws and peaceableness attributed.
Consider the reported relation of law to the limitations of an era.
Retain the Arabic Bayan’s particular account of measures.
Read shared action under command in the Book of Reckoning.
Hear the Bab’s injunction to follow the revealed Book.
Keep the Bab’s derivative rulings and khums instruction in their own setting.
shortened: As for what thou didst desire regarding the derivative laws, take all that thou hast understood from Our allusions, and concerning that which thy knowledge encompasseth not, act according to what hath been revealed in the traditions to the utmost degree. We have not neglected anything in the Book.

As for what you asked about taking certain properties from the believers, both men and women - know that for the fifth (khums) among people, half is the right of the assured believers in this Cause [from the descendants of Hashim] and half is the right of the Imam, peace be upon him.

order.why: Read the livestock ordinance within its stated conditions.
Retain the Bab’s permissions concerning clothing and congregational prayer.
Consider the Bab’s statement about where rulings are to be received.
Keep the Book of Resurrection’s distinctive account of power and knowledge.
Read the reported objection to a new religious law within the imprisonment narrative.
shortened:
He shineth from the Horizon of the Heaven of true Knowledge 
with Wisdom and Utterance!

O Hasan! Hearken unto the Call of Husayn Who hath been incarcerated in the Prison Fortress of 'Akka by reason of that which the hands of the heedless have wrought. If one were to question them, "by what reason have ye imprisoned Him?", they would reply: "Verily, He hath come with a new Shariah and this new Shariah doth not accord with the Law under which we have been. To this matter testifieth our Book which is called the Qur'an, a Book that is from God, the Lord of all mankind.

order.why: Hear the account of the Most Holy Book being revealed amid trials.
Read the text’s own claim for the Kitab-i-Aqdas in its polemical setting.
Consider the inquiries that precede the revelation of laws.
Read delayed circulation and the instruction that Huququ’llah be offered freely.
shortened: The Kitab-i-Aqdas, which was sent down from the holy heaven in previous years, remained concealed for a time and He did not command that it be sent to other lands. He stated that the ordinance of Huququ'llah was revealed in that Book, and this was due to God's mercy and kindness, for after the servants became aware of what the All-Merciful had revealed therein, compliance with it would become obligatory upon all.
However, He commanded that no one should request the Huquq. It is prescribed in the Book of God for each soul to pay it of their own accord with the utmost joy and delight.

order.why: Keep the particular restriction on disclosure in its historical circumstances.
Hear the invitation to look into and ponder the Book.
Read the Book through joy, insight, and concealed wisdom.
Consider its revelation in prison and the benefits the text attributes to it.
shortened: We have revealed in the prison a Book named at the Throne the Most Holy Book, wherein We have laid down the laws and adorned it with the commandments of thy Lord, Who commandeth all in the heavens and earth. Say: O people, hold fast unto it and observe what hath been sent down therein of the wondrous laws of your Lord, the Forgiving, the Generous. It profiteth you in this world and the next, and purifieth you from that which beseemeth you not.

order.why: Retain the concise call to act upon its manifest commandments.
Read the relationship of the Most Holy Book and the Book of the Covenant.
shortened: The Book that abrogates all previous scriptures and books is the Most Holy Book, which is the foundation of the Preserved Tablet of the Covenant, and the Book of the Covenant is its interpreter and expositor.

order.why: Clarify authority through the distinction between receiving and imposing duties.
Keep the reported account of foundational law and additional legislation.
Read the reminder that ordinances also occur in other Tablets.
Consider obligation in relation to the disclosure of laws.
Read the related distinction between initial acceptance and subsequent observance.
shortened: At the beginning of the Cause, God - glorified be His majesty - regarded acceptance alone, for before the revelation of divine ordinances and laws, He revealed and cast forth the Word. Whosoever accepted it without hesitation attained unto all good. But after the heaven of divine decree was raised up and the sun of the Cause shone forth, it became binding and obligatory upon all to hold fast unto it and act according to it.

order.why: Keep the instruction about implementation within its stated historical conditions.
Read the relation of practice to danger, obstacles, and wisdom.
Consider the specific explanation concerning shaving the head and pilgrimage.
Retain the prohibition concerning entry to the Sanctuary in its own setting.
shortened: However, should anyone venture forth after the supreme prohibition, his deed will never be accepted, and should he enter the Most Great Sanctuary he hath been and shall remain deprived, inasmuch as his harm extendeth to the very Root of the Divine Tree and the Branches of the Lordly Tree.

order.why: Keep the brief reference to a stringent command without supplying an unstated object.
shortened: This is one of the stringent and inescapable commandments to neglect which would draw down the wrathful indignation of Almighty God.

order.why: Read the requested tract as a means of informing believers about laws.
Keep the reported claim about Ramadan attributed rather than presenting it as a current observation.
Read the relation of the Fast of the Bayan to the Kitab-i-Aqdas.
Clarifies the relation of the laws of the Bayan to the Kitab-i-Aqdas.
Retain the concise instruction concerning zakat.
Read the related instruction pending detailed assessment limits.
Consider the distinction between expenses and produce in the zakat explanation.
Read the detailed rules concerning travel, communication, support, and absent spouses.
shortened: At the time of departure from home and spouse, it is incumbent upon every soul to set an appointed time for the journey, and whatever time is set shall be binding and effective. If one returns at the appointed time, then verily he hath fulfilled his promise and followed the command of his Lord. If one does not return at the appointed time due to a specific excuse - that is, if some obstacle prevents return such that one is truly impeded - then one must send word and strive with utmost effort to return. If one does not return at the appointed time and sends no word, then the spouse must wait nine months, after which, if she wishes to take another husband, there is no objection. The maintenance of the spouse during this appointed period must be provided.

order.why: Keep the particular marriage instruction in its original religious and historical wording.
shortened: Since, however, this matter is connected with the Law of God, this servant cannot breathe a word. For according to the binding injunction of the Book, ere entering upon one's fifteenth year marriage is not permitted.

order.why: Consider the obligations surrounding found property.
Read the instruction to seek treatment together with its affirmation of divine healing.
Keep the reported expression of mercy toward an attacker beside the limits named in the Book.
Hear the call to diligent observance and its promised spiritual fruit.
Consider the text’s account of progress and salvation.
Read inward nearness through acting upon commandments.
shortened: This pertains to the outward realm; in the inward realm, whosoever hath acted according to the divine commandments and held fast to the Most Holy Book which hath been sent down from the holy Kingdom, is reckoned before God as one of the people of the divine presence.

order.why: Hear the image of laws as stars in the heaven of knowledge.
Retain the instruction to communicate the Book’s ordinances.
shortened: Then command the people to observe what We have sent down from Our holy dominion in Our Most Holy Book, that they may act according to what hath been revealed therein of the ordinances of thy Lord, the All-Knowing.

order.why: Read detachment from the world beside practice.
shortened: Cast the world behind you, then act according to what We have commanded you in Our Most Holy Book. Verily it hath been sent down from the heaven of the Will of your Lord, the Mighty, the Inaccessible.

order.why: Hear the call to steadfastness addressed to believers and believing women.
shortened: We counsel you and those women who have believed in God to show forth the Most Great Steadfastness and to act in accordance with what We have sent down in the Most Holy Book. By the life of God! It is verily a perspicuous Book.

order.why: Retain the concise instruction to act according to the Book.
shortened: Act thou according to what hath been sent down in My Most Holy Book. By My life! It shall profit thee.

order.why: Consider observance as gratitude for a gift.
shortened: And in gratitude for this bounty, which is an effect of the grace of His Holiness the One, you must arise to obey the divine commands and ordinances.

order.why: Read the contrast between following commandments and remaining occupied with desire.
Hear the caution against abandoning the bounds of God.
shortened: Beware lest ye cast behind your backs the bounds of God. Act ye according to that which ye have been commanded by the True One, the Knower of things unseen.

order.why: Consider laws through the image of a strengthened structure.
shortened: Through Our laws the edifice of the Cause hath been made firm and every lofty house hath been raised up.

order.why: Read the association between the Book, character, and good deeds.
shortened: The Supreme Pen hath at all times counseled His loved ones to praiseworthy character and goodly deeds, and hath informed all of the Most Holy Book which hath been sent down from the sacred Kingdom. Blessed is he who holdeth fast unto it and woe unto those who remain veiled from it.

order.why: Join pondering an ordinance with acting upon it.
shortened: There is no doubt that the divine commandments have ever been the cause of salvation for all peoples. Blessed is the one who hath pondered the divine ordinances and acted upon them.

order.why: Consider improvement through loving counsel.
shortened: God willing, the deficient and imperfect souls must become perfect through the loving counsels of those who seek the Ka'bih of their heart's desire, and they must not transgress the divine commandments.

order.why: Hear the appeal to value the present opportunity for action.
shortened: Say: O friends! Know ye the value of the days of the All-Merciful and act according to that which ye have been commanded in the Book.

order.why: Read the dependence of spiritual attainment on lived observance.
Retain the concise appeal to hold fast to divine laws.
shortened: Hold fast unto that which hath been sent down of the laws from the presence of God, the Single, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

order.why: Consider commands and prohibitions through nearness and the removal of veils.
Keep the personal address to Abdu’l-Husayn in its own voice.
shortened: O 'Abdu'l-Husayn! Hold fast to the Book of God and what hath been sent down therein of laws and ordinances.

order.why: Hear the prayer for gathering around divine law.
shortened: Gather them, then, together around this Divine Law, the covenant of which Thou hast established with all Thy Prophets and Thy Messengers, and Whose ordinances Thou hast written down in Thy Tablets and Thy Scriptures.

order.why: Read remembrance, praise, and action within one petition.
Consider submission and trust through the prayer’s images of healing.
shortened: Ask whatsoever thou wishest of Him alone; seek whatsoever thou seekest from Him alone.

With a look He granteth a hundred thousand hopes, with a glance He healeth a hundred thousand incurable ills, with a nod He layeth balm on every wound, with a glimpse He freeth the hearts from the shackles of grief.

He doeth as He doeth, and what recourse have we? He carrieth out His Will, He ordaineth what He pleaseth. Then better for thee to bow down thy head in submission, and put thy trust in the All-Merciful Lord.

order.why: Retain the Book of Certitude’s concise statement of submission.
Hear willing surrender in the Long Obligatory Prayer.
shortened: Thine is the command at all times, O Thou Who art the Lord of all names; and mine is resignation and willing submission to Thy will, O Creator of the heavens!

order.why: Close the linked readings with the reported ship, covenant, and shore analogy.
Read the supplied prayer for the friends’ assistance in following the commands.
Consider the supplied Universal House of Justice passage on tests and spiritual growth.
shortened: Life in this world is a succession of tests and achievements, of falling short and of making new spiritual advances. Sometimes the course may seem very hard, but one can witness, again and again, that the soul who steadfastly obeys the law of Baha'u'llah, however hard it may seem, grows spiritually, while the one who compromises with the law for the sake of his own apparent happiness is seen to have been following a chimera: he does not attain the happiness he sought, he retards his spiritual advance and often brings new problems upon himself.

order.why: End with the supplied question connecting allegiance and the healing of the world.

questions: What changes when law is approached through love, fragrance, healing, or protection?
How do recognition and observance illuminate each other in the Kitab-i-Aqdas passages?
Which examples connect inward conviction with the dignity, property, safety, or happiness of other people?
How does Psalm 119:33–40 link understanding, desire, and wholehearted practice?
What distinctions among revelation, interpretation, legislation, and application become visible across these readings?
How might a community combine steadfast observance with wisdom, loving counsel, and care for those learning to practice?

references.label: 1 · Psalm 119:33–40 · Understanding and delight in the law
references.note: Read the King James Version’s prayer to understand and practice the commandments wholeheartedly. Notice its attention to desire, covetousness, and renewed life. Compare this inward orientation with the compilation’s language of love, joy, and protection, while considering how each tradition connects a spiritual purpose with particular forms of observance.
